rationale: Boone, Glick, and Sahn (2011) analyze cross-sectional household survey data (2004-2005 EPSPAM, 2,190 households across 73 communities in Madagascar) using a conditional logit model of drinking water source choice (public tap, private tap, well, surface water) and a reduced-form Tobit model of individual hours spent fetching water as functions of physical distance to sources, source availability, household wealth/assets, and demographic characteristics. The study does not evaluate any legal, regulatory, tariff/fee, eligibility, procedural, or institutional rule mechanism (explicitly noting in Note 12 that not even fee information was recorded), warranting NONE_NO_RULE_MECHANISM. The central empirical outcomes concern physical accessibility and water-fetching time burden across water sources, placing the outcome squarely in effective_access, and the cross-sectional econometric survey design is observational.
